WHEREAS, the governing body for the City of Cheyenne desires to participate in the
Local Government Project ARPA Grant program to assist infinancing this project;
WHEREAS, the governing body for the City of Cheyenne recognizes the need for the
Project;
WHEREAS, the Local Government ARPA Grant program requires that certain criteria be
met, as described in the State Loan and Investment Board’s Rules and Regulations governing the
WHEREAS, the governing body for the City of Cheyenne requests a grant of up to
$1,900,000 for the cost of the proposed Project;
WHEREAS, the governing body for the City of Cheyenne agrees to provide up to
$1,900,000 from the 5th Penny Sales Tax for the required local match; and,
NOW, THEREFORE, BE IT RESOLVED BY THE GOVERNING BODY OF THE
CITYOF CHEYENNE, WYOMING, that a grant application requesting up to$1,900,000.00be
submittedto the State Loan and Investment Board, for consideration to State Loan and
Investment Board meeting to assist in funding the Van Buren Avenue Flood Control project.
BE IT FURTHER RESOLVED, that Thomas Cobb, City Engineer is hereby designated
as the authorized representative of the City of Cheyenne to act onbehalf of the governing body
on all matters relating to this funding application.

Van Buren Avenue Storm Sewer Interceptor Project
City of Cheyenne
9:
ARPA Justification for Water Projects
Insupportof the City of Cheyenne's application for the Van Buren Avenue Storm water Sewer
under the Treasury's Final Rule.
A. Detailed description of the how the project responds to an identified need to achieve or
maintain an adequate minimum level of service
As Cheyenne continues to expand, the need for affordable housing is becoming
critical.The projectarea has been identified for infrastructure development for the safety of
residents and businesses.Stormwater drainage is critical to mitigate flood risk and toreduce
the amount of runoff and runoff pollution The project areais alsolocated within afederally
designated Opportunity Zone. Stormwater mitigation for this area will facilitate continued
economic growth.
B. Explanation of how the proposed project willprovide an adequate minimum level of
service
Our proposed storm sewer interceptor will be designed for the50-year storm
event providing the best benefit-cost over other storm frequencies evaluated forthe storm
drainage system.The 50-year design provides significantly more flood protection for our benefit
area andwill positively impact the east side of Cheyenne.
C. Explanation of how the project is cost effective
As stated above, acursory benefit-cost evaluation was completed for a range of
storm frequencies and themost cost-effective approach was determined tobea50-year storm
event protection for the proposed storm sewer interceptor.The 50-year design combined with the
storm drainage conveyance capacity within the street curb&gutter sections of the design
corridor will provide a high level of flood protection for the benefit area.
D.Explanation of how the project will be maintained
All stormwater sewer systems including inlets and lateral piping and detention
storage outlet structures are routinely inspected and maintained by City of Cheyenne
construction staff inspectors and Public Works staff Moreover s a par of the City sM
Stormwater Management Plan (SWMP), the City also contracts work out to assist with the
overall maintenance of our stormwater system.
